summary.one_liner: SCons is an open-source software construction tool that determines which parts of a project need rebuilding and runs the commands to build them, with configuration written as Python scripts.
summary.what_it_does: SCons reads Python-based configuration files and works out which components must be built or rebuilt, then invokes the necessary commands. It includes built-in dependency analysis for C, C++ and FORTRAN, with user-defined Scanners for other languages. It has built-in Builders for C, C++, D, Java, FORTRAN, Yacc, Lex, Qt, SWIG, TeX and LaTeX, and user-defined Builders can be added for other file types. It detects changes using cryptographic hashes (timestamps optional), supports parallel builds, and can share built files through a cache. It also generates Microsoft Visual Studio project files and offers Autoconf-like checks for headers, libraries, functions and typedefs.
use_cases: compiling C or C++ projects with automatic dependency tracking
replacing Makefiles with Python build scripts
cross-platform builds on Linux, Windows, macOS and other POSIX systems
generating Visual Studio project files from a build
sharing build artifacts through a cache to speed up builds
how_to_run: scons  (run in a project directory that has an SConstruct file)
stack: Microsoft Visual C++ compiler (default on Windows)
gfortran, cc and c++ (default compilers on non-Windows systems)
notable: Build configuration is written as ordinary Python scripts rather than a domain-specific language
Automatic dependency analysis for C, C++ and FORTRAN without a separate make depend step
Reproducible builds when SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is set
Global view of all dependencies, so no multiple build passes are needed
caveats: Requires Python 3.9 or higher; older Python versions are supported only by earlier releases (4.11.0 for 3.7/3.8)
Some experimental features need extra packages, such as the ninja package for the Ninja feature
Bug-fix pull requests are normally applied only to the main branch, so older releases generally do not get fixes
